steps.name: Frantic Girl
steps.text: Raise that lamp a little higher, I need the light on every detail of the exhibits.

spans.text: Raise that lamp a little higher, I need the light on

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: Yes, Curator Hanimefendi!

steps.name: Frantic Girl
steps.text: Who put this statue of a songstress with the sculptures from the Old Calendar Age of Shadows? Completely wrong era. Take it out and move it to Hall Two.

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: I'm on it, Curator Hanimefendi!

steps.name: Frantic Girl
steps.text: Where is that instrument restored with tech from the Old Calendar Age of Chants? Why don't I see it?

spans.text: is that instrument restored with tech from the Old Calendar Age of Chants? Why don't I see it?

steps.name: Frantic Girl
steps.text: Not here...

steps.name: Frantic Girl
steps.text: Not here either...

steps.name: Cheery Singing
steps.text: ♪O guests from afar, ripples in the lotus pond follow thee here♪

steps.name: Cheery Singing
steps.text: ♪Neath the tree's shade, sup sweet dates and fresh beer♪

steps.name: Cheery Singing
steps.text: ♪Let us toast now to a midsummer, and cheers!♪

steps.name: Sycophantic Employee
steps.text: Oh, Medjehtiqedti Hanimefendi, your singing rivals even the most elegant of fowlbeasts! I can't tear myself away!

steps.name: Ingratiating Employee
steps.text: Ah, Medjehtiqedti Hanimefendi, the notes of your lute flow like purest water! Like the calmest, sweetest brook!

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: But of course. I have worked tirelessly for months to produce the perfect rendition of this ancient ballad.

steps.name: Frantic Girl
steps.text: Hmph. Words sweet as honey, fingers idle as a slumberfoot. No wonder I couldn't find you.

steps.name: Frantic Girl
steps.text: You do know that restored lute is going on display tomorrow, right, Titi?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Do allow the welcoming committee to borrow it for today, Anat. We have an honored guest coming, and the museum must receive her well.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: It's a special exhibit for the Flood Festival, Titi.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Our top priority is ensuring there are no errors in any of the sections.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Our visitors can be very fussy about the details. You've been here long enough, you should know better than I.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Let's not get mad now, Curator Hanimefendi.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: This is your first major exhibit since taking up your post, so I understand that you're a little anxious about it.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: But trust me, Anat, you need to calm down. No matter what you're putting on display, someone is going to nitpick it.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: This is Menat-Ha'mait. Every family's got some treasure stashed away somewhere. It's no surprise they'd turn their noses up at our exhibits.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: I'm going to check over the new displays for tomorrow.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Don't worry, I won't disturb your date with that esteemed gentleman.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: It's an object I'm studying, not my date.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: You look at it ever so lovingly, though.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Strange...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Has no-one picked her up yet since we've been talking?

steps.name: Extremely Idle Citizen
steps.text: I'm guessing that girl over there is learning how the irrigation channels work, gonna write a thesis on the history of it.

steps.name: Incredibly Bored Citizen
steps.text: Or maybe she's an epigraphist, and she's just cleaning the sludge off the stele in the river.

steps.name: Extremely Idle Citizen
steps.text: What's the difference? They're just different types of history nerd.

steps.name: Extremely Idle Citizen
steps.text: Blame it on the city's long history. Every historian in Sargon gets obsessed with this place.

steps.name: Incredibly Bored Citizen
steps.text: Yeah. Look at this ancient riverway we've got here, four centuries old, broad and wide. And our buildings? A youthful two centuries, yet tall and impressive.

steps.name: Incredibly Bored Citizen
steps.text: You wanna talk about 'rich historical tradition'? Well, here you have it.

steps.name: Extremely Idle Citizen
steps.text: Can any of them beat the Flood Festival, though? We've been celebrating it for over a thousand years.

steps.name: Incredibly Bored Citizen
steps.text: Oh, when it floods, I'm going to offer up some white oasis flowers to the river god. May His breath be forever filled with their fragrant aroma.

steps.name: Incredibly Bored Citizen
steps.text: What offering have you prepared, friend?

steps.name: Extremely Idle Citizen
steps.text: A cup and plate of pure gold, along with a jar of wine, in accordance with my family traditions. The wine was sealed by my grandfather when my father was born, an excellent vintage.

steps.name: Extremely Idle Citizen
steps.text: May He enjoy its taste, and share in the festival spirit with us.

steps.name: Incredibly Bored Citizen
steps.text: May we meet Him wandering the realm, and earn His blessing.

steps.name: Incredibly Bored Citizen
steps.text: O immortal Menat-Ha'mait, may He forever grace this city.

steps.name: Girl by the Shore
steps.text: Did you find it yet, hanimefendi?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Give me a sec, kiddo, I think I felt it just now.

steps.name: Girl by the Shore
steps.text: But you've been standing in the river for half an hour already. You keep saying you almost got it...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Shh! I'm trying to concentrate here...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Seriously, where has our little shahzada run off to now?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I've got people at every gate waiting, but none of them have seen her.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I've put so much thought into welcoming you, how could I let you just slip into the city like this?

steps.name: Happy Lady
steps.text: Masaa al-kheir, Medjehtiqedti Hanimefendi. Wherever are you going in such a hurry?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Ah, Bekti Hanimefendi, it's you. I'm meeting an old friend of mine!

steps.name: Happy Lady
steps.text: Here, some oranges I just plucked from my garden. They ripened just before the festival, I'm sure everyone will love them.

steps.name: Happy Lady
steps.text: Take a few for your friend, Medjehtiqedti Hanimefendi.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: She's not a fan of favors, but I thank you in her stead. Salaam, Bekti Hanimefendi.

steps.name: Happy Lady
steps.text: Ma'a s-salaama!

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: The people here are so friendly.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: *sigh* Let me have a think about where she'd go...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Where did she like to run off back when we were in school?

steps.name: Foreign Traveler
steps.text: Ah, I'm really sorry, hanim! I didn't see you there. Forgive me for knocking your oranges on the ground.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I'm fine, how about you? Are you alright?

steps.name: Foreign Traveler
steps.text: Thank you for your kindness, hanim.

steps.name: Foreign Traveler
steps.text: Oh no...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: What's with the frown all of a sudden? Are you hurt?

steps.name: Foreign Traveler
steps.text: A shadow flitted across your forehead just now, an ill omen. I fear you will meet with some misfortune soon.

steps.name: Foreign Traveler
steps.text: If you are willing to part with five dinars, I can ward it off for you.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Umm... Well, uh, sorry, but I've got an appointment, gotta go now! Bye!

steps.name: Foreign Traveler
steps.text: Wait! Two dinars! Just two dinars, then!

steps.name: Foreign Traveler
steps.text: This isn't a trick! You really are about to run into some bad luck!

steps.name: Girl by the Shore
steps.text: You wouldn't trick me, would you...?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Of course not. I always keep my word.

steps.name: Girl by the Shore
steps.text: Really? *sniff* But...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Aw, don't cry, I'll—

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Agh! It slipped away again!

steps.name: Sad Girl
steps.text: Waaaaaahhh!

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Ah, no, don't cry! I was just teasing you! I got it! See? It's right here in my hand!

steps.name: Sad Girl
steps.text: You're a meanie...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: *sigh* I'm too used to teasing my little brother back home.

steps.name: Sad Girl
steps.text: I feel sorry for your poor little brother...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Save your pity, that kid gives me endless headaches. Alright, pass me the jar. I'll put the fin in it for you.

steps.name: Sobbing Girl
steps.text: I thought I'd never see my goldfin again... Thanks, hanimefendi.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Tsk, tsk, tsk. I worked my butt off helping you get your finny friend back. Put a little more pep into that 'thanks'.

steps.name: Sobbing Girl
steps.text: THANK YOU SO MUCH! YOU'RE THE BEST!

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Now that's more like it.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Alright, you'd best hurry home already. No more fancy ideas about trying to take your pet for a walk.

steps.name: Happy Girl
steps.text: See you, hanimefendi.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Taking a pet fin for a walk in the river? Reminds me of the crazy ideas I had as a kid.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: *cough*

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Well then. Seems our audience has finally had enough of me groping around in the water for finbeasts.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Glad you still know me so well, Pepe.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: *sigh* I really don't want to head to the museum so soon. When Anat's in question-asking mode, I won't even get a moment's rest.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Where is she, anyway? She didn't come with you?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: She's acting curator now. Got a lot of things to do. With the upcoming super-important exhibition, she's been busier than ever.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Nice. Never thought she'd get promoted right after she arrived. I remember back in school, nobody thought she'd go far with that meek personality, but I knew she was a hard worker. She'll go far.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: She's always been one tough reed. She never yields.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Sure you aren't talking about yourself? You've been in this city for a while. No big changes?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Me? I'm not too busy, but I'm also not too free. I was just barely able to secure the title of vice curator.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Weren't you in charge of stuff at that Columbian museum?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I was in charge of their business operations. Things are different here, you know.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: The Menat-Ha'mait museum doesn't need to profit. Annual support from the Lords Ameer and the Padishahs is enough. No use for me.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Which is great. I get to take it easy.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: But you always kept yourself busy... back in the day.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: How about you? You must have gotten a lot of good stuff out of your travels.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: More than you can imagine.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Hmm. Sounds like your report's going to be a lot longer than you can imagine as well.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Oh no. It's so hot here. Feel like I've got sunstroke. I'm gonna stay here and cool down in the breeze.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Save it. Do you know how many times I used that excuse to help you ditch class?

steps.name: Waiter
steps.text: You've been sitting there quite a while, hanim, and the sun is rather fierce. Would you like something to drink? We have our specialty liquorice juice, freshly made. Only five dinars.

steps.name: Waiter
steps.text: Or how about an apple and roselle tea? Two dinars a cup.

steps.name: Odd Woman
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Waiter
steps.text: Perhaps a glass of apricot juice then? Only one dinar.

steps.name: Odd Woman
steps.text: I said no.

steps.name: Waiter
steps.text: Very well then...

steps.name: Extravagant Traveler
steps.text: Hold on, waiter, not so fast. A pot of your best coffee, if you will, and add some local cardamom and cloves.

steps.name: Extravagant Traveler
steps.text: And a glass of liquorice juice for the lady.

steps.name: Waiter
steps.text: Right away.

steps.name: Extravagant Traveler
steps.text: Coming to Menat-Ha'mait for the Flood Festival, anyone should have filled their wallet. You won't get much out of your trip like this.

steps.name: Extravagant Traveler
steps.text: No offense, but I have always been of the belief that man should live within his means. If your funds are insufficient, there are plenty more other places to enjoy a holiday.

steps.name: Extravagant Traveler
steps.text: I've heard that Dossoles in Bolívar is rather pleasant. Cheap, with beautiful scenery, suitable for those of more... frugal means.

steps.name: Odd Woman
steps.text: You speak wisdom. A truly educated man you must be.

steps.name: Extravagant Traveler
steps.text: You flatter me. And yourself? Broadening your horizons on the road?

steps.name: Odd Woman
steps.text: On the road...? I suppose so. I seek my own road to follow.

steps.name: Waiter
steps.text: Your coffee, effendi.

steps.name: Extravagant Traveler
steps.text: Here, please.

steps.name: Waiter
steps.text: Your liquorice juice, hanim.

steps.name: Odd Woman
steps.text: (Drinks it up in a single gulp)

steps.name: Odd Woman
steps.text: I thank you for your hospitality.

steps.name: Extravagant Traveler
steps.text: (Quietly) Hmph.

steps.name: Extravagant Traveler
steps.text: Waiter, could you tell me of some particularly fun activities during your Flood Festival—

steps.name: Extravagant Traveler
steps.text: Why the look?

steps.name: Waiter
steps.text: Forgive me, effendi. I am simply amazed that the hanim was so hesitant to part with her money for a drink, yet gave me a sizable tip...

steps.name: Extravagant Traveler
steps.text: Ah, it appears my fellow traveler was of small means but great pride.

steps.name: Extravagant Traveler
steps.text: No matter, I shall find some amusements by myself. The bill please, waiter.

steps.name: Waiter
steps.text: Fifteen dinars in total, effendi.

steps.name: Waiter
steps.text: Effendi?

steps.name: Extravagant Traveler
steps.text: Err... Wherever has my coin-purse gone?

steps.name: Odd Woman
steps.text: May the river wash away these gilded scraps of metal. May those who need them find them as its waters rise.

steps.name: Odd Woman
steps.text: Enough time wasted. I nearly lost sight of my target.

steps.name: Odd Woman
steps.text: I've heard the City of Radiance is adorned in jewels, and that countless brave souls have sought out its treasures without success.

steps.name: Odd Woman
steps.text: And so I walked the long road and arrived here, only to find miser after miser bickering over a few gold coins.

A dark cloud floats by, blocking the glaring rays of the sun. The red-maned woman pours coins out of her purse, tossing them into the river with an even hand. The ripples tear apart the sun's reflection.
Then she disappears into the crowd, whistling.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Ahh... The Grand Bazaar's apricot juice still hits the spot. Tastes pretty much the same as it did back when we were in school!

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: This is where I thought you'd be, but it took me some long, fruitless searching to remember that we would only ever come here the three of us.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: When you were alone, you would always go to...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: The river. I love strolling along the river by myself. Didn't think you'd run all over the place to find me.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: You are an honored guest, Pepe.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: We're friends, you don't need to be so particular about all this...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: You didn't organize some toe-curlingly cringey performance to welcome me back, did you?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: That would be the proper rites and ceremonies.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Save it! I can hear the cogs in your brain grinding away as you cook up your evil machinations.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: So what big discovery got you coming back here?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: A jewel.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: A jewel?

steps.name: Gem Merchant
steps.text: Sapphire bracelets, necklaces and earrings, make a set of your choosing, only two thousand dinars a set! If you like it then buy it, no haggling, no bargaining. Only two thousand dinars and they're yours!

steps.name: Streetside Loudspeaker
steps.text: Dear customers, we are now offering a lovely selection of hand-selected emerald rings. Enjoy a discount if you buy an entire box!

steps.name: Streetside Loudspeaker
steps.text: Guaranteed quality and weight, while still economical. Every one fifteen carats! Buy some to send home to your family and friends, only four thousand five hundred dinars for the box!

steps.name: TV Advertisement
steps.text: Rubies, sapphires, chrysoberyl, amethysts, rose quartz, olivine! For gems, come to the Grand Bazaar, where we offer bulk trade and low prices, all day every day!

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Menat-Ha'mait's drowning in all sorts of jewels. I don't think you're turning heads if it's any regular old gem.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Hey, this jewel's pretty extraordinary, okay?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Extraordinary?

steps.name: Lady of Refined Taste
steps.text: I recently bought a piece of pink kyanite. They say it was once used for purifying water. The Originium circuit carved into it is incredibly delicate, a work of art in its own right.

steps.name: Ornately-Dressed Man
steps.text: Sounds rather valuable. I bought a similar tourmaline just last month. The power of my Arts improved substantially after laying it into my cane.

steps.name: Impressively Stylish Elder
steps.text: Both cannot compare with this treasure of mine. Look.

steps.name: Lady of Refined Taste
steps.text: Isn't this a limited edition gemstone belt from last year? I remember the peddler said it could rejuvenate your skin and slow your aging.

steps.name: Ornately-Dressed Man
steps.text: Do you feel anything wearing it?

steps.name: Impressively Stylish Elder
steps.text: I do feel rather more refreshed...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Eh, compared to the ones going around the Grand Bazaar, the one I found can do something really special.

spans.text: Eh, compared to the ones going around the Grand Bazaar, the one I found can do something

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Special how? These Originium-etched jewels being sold here are already pretty special for anyone coming from outside the city.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Let's get walking first, Titi.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Don't tell me there's some kind of dirty secret behind it?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: No way! Relax, I'll tell you, but—

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Before this scorcher of a sun gets too high in the sky, I want to run by Septagram Avenue to buy an idol. Even research needs the blessing of the gods, right?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: You best walk quick then. That road's going to be too hot for your feet real soon.

steps.name: Shady Woman
steps.text: The target is moving toward the museum in the heart of the city...

steps.name: Shady Woman
steps.text: Considering she was personally welcomed by the vice-curator, it appears my information was correct. She is no ordinary woman.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: What?! The jewel you found was a relic of the Shah?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Man... I shouldn't have worn open-toed sandals. I'm going to have sandal-patterned feet later.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Seriously? You're thinking about your sandals now? Where did you find that jewel?

spans.text: now? Where did you find that jewel?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I got a clue in a place once known as Szubat-Arsalan. After a few twists and turns, I finally found it in the territory of a Lord Ameer.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: The Lionpride's Ancient Throne...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I also saw some ancient images left by the Shah himself in a cave full of crystals.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: And I wrote everything down in this journal. It'll make public the true location of the great trove, and prove that the Shah's promise to the Nightzmora was more than just a legend.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Just think what might be waiting for us among all those riches?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Yet no matter how valuable that stuff may be, the true treasure is the clues that will help us reconstruct the truth of that era.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: We'll find the answers to the Shah's unsolved mysteries one by one, Titi!

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Why would he make such a crazy declaration of war? Or what really happened in the legendary clash with Kharanduu Khagan in the south! Or his final resting place!

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: These discoveries will shock the people! All Shar-Agade, the entire City of Gold, will be looking my way!

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: If you know where it is, just take a team there to excavate it. It's just—

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: No, there's one last trail to follow. I need to borrow an artifact from the museum.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: You're the daughter of a Padishah. The museum storehouses are open to you, anything you want that isn't on public display.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Thaaaaat's the issue.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Wait. Don't tell me you want...
Pepe looks at the facade of the museum, a banner slowly unfolding across it.
The banner depicts a slender mummy draped in golden armor, its face hidden by a death mask.
And at the end of that banner is written in great, big script:
Landmark Exhibit Commemorating Varjavandabad Museum's Anniversary—The Nameless General of the Shah's Very Court!

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: The General? No, he is the guardian of the trove.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: No matter who it actually is, it's Anat's most prized exhibit. I don't think you're going to borrow it that easily.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Well, a jewel with clues won't prove anything by itself. I can only show my worth to my father and the Shahanshah by finding the Shah's trove.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: If I do that, I can go to the City of Gold, become the Shahanshah's Historian of Shar-Agade, and write an account of all Sargonian history.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Being a Padishah's heir not good enough for you, Pepe?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: The wealth and authority is just superficial prosperity. The true honor that runs through our family is the role of court historian, passed down from generation to generation.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: But... Hasn't your father always wanted your brother to be the court historian?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Well, we both have the same basic qualities. But I'm not losing to him on ability either.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Pepe, the City of Gold's envoy is taking your brother there in two months.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I'll make it in time, Titi! I just need you to help me! Anat's only willing to lend me that mummy to study come autumn.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: But this summer is my last opportunity. I can't wait that long.

spans.text: opportunity. I can't wait that long.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: You and your brother... You were always fighting as kids, and now you're at loggerheads over the same court appointment.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: ...Here. My pass. Take it.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: You can sneak into the exhibition hall at night and study it, quietly.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Titi...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I'm just sick of seeing you two bicker and quarrel these past few years.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: This is the last time I'll help you. If in the end, you come up empty-handed, then please don't keep stubbornly trudging on.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I won't. I won't come up empty-handed.
Ignoring Pepe's murmuring, Medjehtiqedti stands up to look at the grand edifice, witness to centuries of history.
The sun shines upon all the gardens and buildings, and under the boundless blue sky, the great trapezoid looms over them.
The leaves of tall palm trees besides them rustle in the wind.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: I might see it every day, but I'm still stunned by its grandeur.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: For so long has it quietly guarded the city, fending off time itself in silence.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Yep. A human lifespan is nothing compared to it, no matter how long it may be.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Over in the blink of an eye.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: If only we could stop time for a moment.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Yeah. That would be great.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: See you at the exhibition tomorrow. If you get caught, just say you stole the pass.

steps.name: Odd Woman
steps.text: The exhibition... tomorrow...

steps.name: Odd Woman
steps.text: Good. The guest's itinerary has been confirmed. I'll welcome her properly.

steps.name: Odd Woman
steps.text: A descendant of a glorious clan of historians, the one who spreads ballads of kings and heroes, explorer of all Sargon, purveyor of knowledge, a respected Padishah's daughter—

steps.name: Odd Woman
steps.text: Djerwnapekhaper Saciut Hatshepsut.

steps.name: Odd Woman
steps.text: Any other would worry they would forget all these appellations, but the one who stands here is Narantuya, and her only regret is that these titles are all held by one person.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Fine. I guess the ransom ought to settle my debts even if it's just one girl.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: The money left in this purse should be enough to buy a ticket for tomorrow...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Never mind.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: The line would be too long, and the sun too hot.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: And in this city, gold coins are too common to be worth anything.

steps.name: Minoan Traveler
steps.text: Do you swear by your golden sun, your splendid gems and the great museum behind you?

steps.name: Minoan Traveler
steps.text: That you will answer prudently on account of your respect for history and civilization alike?

steps.name: Minoan Traveler
steps.text: Look within, at your own conscience, and tell me once more. How much is a ticket to the museum?

steps.name: Museum Ticketer
steps.text: I already told you, hanim. The hall for non-Sargonian artifacts is free of charge. Only the Sargonian exhibition hall needs tickets.

steps.name: Museum Ticketer
steps.text: If you don't understand, we have the prices for our tour services here on the window. You can hire one of our translators too, if needed.

steps.name: Minoan Traveler
steps.text: So the Minoan exhibition hall is free to enter?!

steps.name: Museum Ticketer
steps.text: I'll say it once more, hanim. There is no 'Minoan exhibition hall'.

spans.text: I'll say it once more, hanim. There is

steps.name: Museum Ticketer
steps.text: But at times there will be a few Minoan artifacts on display in the Northeastern Tributary exhibit.

steps.name: Minoan Traveler
steps.text: ...'Northeastern Tributary'?
The foreign traveler takes a deep breath, the muscles of her bare arm bulging as she clenches her fist.
A part of the ticketer's mind is telling her to pull the booth's shutter closed, but the traveler's other hand is firmly holding it open.

steps.name: Minoan Traveler
steps.text: History is a grand river beside which all who live upon this great land trek. The Originium workshops of the Ancient Town of Tal'sas were unearthed by Gaulish explorers. The scrolls detailing the legends of old Agamem were restored by Minoan artisans.

steps.name: Minoan Traveler
steps.text: But Minos's own history has gone against the current, and has found itself scattered across the golden sands. I have traced its path just to catch a glimpse of its fragments.

steps.name: Minoan Traveler
steps.text: Whether or not you agree, a historian's mission is to find the past that people have forgotten.

steps.name: Minoan Traveler
steps.text: For the sake of this duty, should we not prevent arrogant discrimination by history's tyrannical plunderers?

steps.name: Minoan Traveler
steps.text: In other words, if you believe that Sargonian history is worth a hundred dinars to see, then should Minoan history not stand equal?

steps.name: Museum Ticketer
steps.text: Do you want a ticket or not, hanim?

steps.name: Minoan Traveler
steps.text: —Even more importantly, Sargonians, as it so happens, are the plunderers, in this case.

steps.name: Minoan Traveler
steps.text: With all that said, are you willing to hold fast to your conscience and confront the true value of Minos's artifacts?

steps.name: Museum Ticketer
steps.text: Next!

steps.name: Minoan Traveler
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Minoan Traveler
steps.text: My name is Aspasia ho Herias. Please, use the Minoan spelling, not a Sargonian transliteration.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: A ticket, if you would so please.
